title: Flow Graph [docs]
description: added description for the Flow Graph window + screenshot

notes.body: hi @Lekensteyn - I used the cap file for HTTP/2 you've provided previously to get the screenshot for this menu if that's ok. Could you please review this? thanks!

This section needs to be expanded by a lot:

- The text mentions "client and server", but it might be better to speak of "endpoints" or "hosts". Every vertical line represents a host.
- The number on the side of a horizontal line represents the port number.
- The time on the left is not "duration", but the packet time. This is the same time format as used in the main packet list and can be controlled through View -> Time Display Format. Changing this format requires reopening the Flow Graph option though.
- One can click on a horizontal arrow or flow to select the packet in the packet list.
- There are many keyboard shortcuts which can be found by right-clicking the graph. These should be documented.
hi @Lekensteyn - I applied your suggestions. check it please? )

 === Flow Graph
 
-{missing}
+The Flow Graph window shows connections between hosts. It displays the packet time, direction, ports and comments for each captured connection. You can filter all connections by ICMP Flows, ICMPv6 Flows, UIM Flows and TCP Flows.
+
+.Flow Graph window
+image::wsug_graphics/ws-flow-graph.png[{screenshot-attrs}]
+
+Each vertical line represents the specific host, which you can see in the top of the window.
+
+The numbers in each row at the very left of the window represent the time packet. You can change the time format in the menu:View[Time Display Format]. If you change the time format, you must relaunch the Flow Graph window to observe the time in a new format.
+
+The numbers at the both ends of each arrow between hosts represent the port numbers.
+
+Left-click a row to select a corresponding packet in the packet list.
+
+Right-click on the graph for additional options, such as selecting the previous, current, or next packet in the packet list. This menu also contains shortcuts for moving the diagram.
